children: Falling oil prices are helping send U.S. stocks higher this morning.

All three indexes opened in the green Tuesday, with the tech-focused Nasdaq leading the way. Brent crude futures are down more than 2% at roughly $98 a barrel after encouraging news about oil exports from the Middle East.

Saudi Arabia is running tests on its East-West pipeline and could restart flows as early as this week. The pipeline, a crucial route circumventing Hormuz, was recently closed after drone attacks. Japan's Kyodo News Agency separately reported that Iran has proposed to reopen the Strait of Hormuz if the U.S. lifts its blockade.

President Trump is expected to address world leaders this morning at the United Nations General Assembly in New York. Investors also are eyeing whether a meeting between Trump and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian will materialize after Trump said over the weekend that he is "probably" open to it.

Global government bond yields are following oil prices lower. The 10-year yield is trading around 4.95%. Stocks tied to the artificial-intelligence trade are mixed after an enthusiastic reception for Meta's new AI agent lifted the sector Monday.
Write to Caitlin McCabe at caitlin.mccabe@wsj.com
